articles.title: Critical Zimbra Flaw Could Let Crafted Emails Run Malicious Code in User Sessions
articles.summary: Zimbra is warning users of a critical stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its Classic Web Client that enables arbitrary code execution via malicious emails. Users are urged to apply the latest security updates immediately, as the flaw currently lacks a CVE identifier.

articles.title: No Manners Here: The Ruthless Rise of The Gentlemen Ransomware
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports on the emergence and rapid expansion of The Gentlemen ransomware, highlighting its reliance on an affiliate-based business model. The analysis details how this operational structure is driving the group's increased threat level.

articles.title: Update Now: Critical Zimbra Classic Web Client Flaw Could Expose Mailboxes
articles.summary: Zimbra has released version 10.1.19 to patch a critical stored XSS vulnerability in its Classic Web Client that allows attackers to execute code via malicious emails. Users are advised to update immediately to prevent unauthorized mailbox access.

articles.title: Armenian national pleads guilty to Ryuk ransomware attacks
articles.summary: Karen Vardanyan, an Armenian national, has pleaded guilty to his role in orchestrating Ryuk ransomware attacks. He faces a potential 15-year prison sentence and is required to pay $1.2 million in restitution.

articles.title: Europe revives law allowing big tech to scan for CSAM
articles.summary: The European Parliament has approved 'Chat Control 2.0,' a legislative measure that enables technology companies to scan user messages for child sexual abuse material (CSAM). This mandate forces platforms like Google, Meta, and Microsoft to implement scanning mechanisms, raising significant debates regarding user privacy and encryption.

articles.title: CISA looks to remedy ailments from big May credential leak
articles.summary: CISA has released a forensic report detailing its efforts to enhance security protocols and vulnerability reporting following a significant credential leak in May. The agency is implementing new protections to prevent future unauthorized access to its sensitive data.

articles.title: Destructive Windows backdoor stuffs multiple wipers and ransomware code into a single package
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified a new modular backdoor called GigaWiper that integrates multiple malware families, including wipers and ransomware, into a single destructive package. This tool demonstrates an evolution in multi-functional threat payloads designed to maximize damage during a compromise.

articles.title: Ryuk operator pleads guilty; Blackcat/AlphV conspirator gets nearly 6-year sentence
articles.summary: Two individuals linked to major ransomware groups, Ryuk and Blackcat/AlphV, have faced significant legal consequences, with one pleading guilty and the other receiving a 70-month prison sentence.

articles.title: License plate cameras may be next target after Supreme Court reins in location tracking
articles.summary: Recent Supreme Court rulings on location tracking have sparked discussions regarding the potential requirement of warrants for Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data. This shift could significantly alter law enforcement surveillance capabilities and data collection practices.

articles.title: URGENT - Progress Tells ShareFile Customers to Shut Down Storage Zone Controllers Over Security Threat
articles.summary: Progress Software has advised ShareFile customers to shut down their Storage Zone Controllers due to a credible external security threat. The company has temporarily disabled access to impacted accounts while investigating the issue.

articles.title: Injective Labs GitHub Compromise Pushes Wallet-Key-Stealing npm Packages
articles.summary: Threat actors compromised the Injective Labs GitHub repository to distribute a malicious version of the @injectivelabs/sdk-ts npm package designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet credentials. This supply chain attack used fake telemetry functionality to exfiltrate private keys and mnemonic phrases from affected users.

articles.title: Six New U-Boot Flaws Could Let Malicious Images Crash Devices or Run Code at Boot
articles.summary: Researchers discovered six vulnerabilities in the U-Boot bootloader that could allow attackers to crash affected devices or execute arbitrary code during the boot process. The flaws impact a wide range of hardware, including routers, cameras, and server management chips.

articles.title: Laser Attack Resets Tangem Wallet Passwords on Cards That Can't Be Patched
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered a hardware-level vulnerability in Tangem crypto wallets that allows an attacker to reset passwords using a precise laser pulse. Because the physical vulnerability cannot be patched, affected devices remain permanently susceptible to unauthorized access if physical possession is obtained.

articles.title: Researcher Details WhatsApp-to-Host Attack Chain Using Three OpenClaw Flaws
articles.summary: Three high-severity security vulnerabilities in the OpenClaw AI assistant have been disclosed, which could allow attackers to perform credential theft, privilege escalation, and arbitrary code execution. These flaws have since been addressed through patches.

articles.title: China, India ran separate spying campaigns against same Pakistani police force
articles.summary: Chinese and Indian state-sponsored actors concurrently compromised the same Pakistani police force systems between February 2024 and April 2026, specifically targeting operations in a region affected by separatist insurgency.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Negotiator Gets 70 Months for Helping BlackCat Extort Victims
articles.summary: Former ransomware negotiator Angelo Martino has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for facilitating BlackCat extortion schemes and misusing confidential client data. The case highlights the legal consequences for individuals who collaborate with ransomware gangs.

articles.title: New MODBEACON RAT Uses gRPC Streaming for Encrypted C2 Traffic
articles.summary: The China-linked threat group Silver Fox is utilizing a new Rust-based remote access trojan called MODBEACON, which leverages gRPC streaming for encrypted command-and-control communication. The group primarily distributes this malware through SEO poisoning and counterfeit software installers.

articles.title: Ransomware Never Stopped: Over 9,000 Confirmed Attacks Since 2018
articles.summary: Between 2018 and 2026, over 9,000 verified ransomware attacks have occurred globally, with the United States remaining the primary target and Qilin identified as a leading threat actor. The data highlights a persistent trend of over 1,400 annual attacks since 2023.

articles.title: Incode brings on-device processing to age estimation for privacy-focused verification
articles.summary: Incode has introduced an on-device age estimation tool that performs identity verification and liveness detection locally to ensure user privacy. This technology helps organizations comply with global age assurance regulations without transmitting sensitive facial data to external servers.

articles.title: Fashion mart Miinto unzips breach details, warns shoppers to watch for phisherfolk
articles.summary: Danish fashion retailer Miinto is notifying customers of a data breach involving its order management system and advising users to remain vigilant against potential phishing attacks.

articles.title: Unpatched XRING Flaw in XQUIC Lets Remote Clients Crash HTTP/3 Servers
articles.summary: A critical, unpatched vulnerability dubbed XRING exists in Alibaba's XQUIC library, allowing remote attackers to crash HTTP/3 servers using a small amount of legitimate QPACK traffic. The flaw requires no authentication or malformed packets to exploit.

articles.title: From 17,000 to 1.1 Million Assets: How Lumen Technologies Rebuilt Exposure Management at Scale
articles.summary: Lumen Technologies successfully overhauled its large-scale asset exposure management strategy to address common discrepancies in enterprise asset inventory data. The case study highlights the importance of consolidating fragmented data to prevent downstream security failures.

articles.title: Exposed Hacker Server Reveals WP-SHELLSTORM Backdooring Thousands of WordPress Sites
articles.summary: A misconfigured server belonging to a cybercrime group has exposed the operational details of a large-scale campaign that compromised thousands of WordPress sites using the WP-SHELLSTORM backdoor. The discovery provides researchers with unique visibility into the internal tools, logs, and target lists used in the mass-hacking operation.

articles.title: Study of 281 Free Android VPN Apps Finds Traffic Leaks, Unencrypted Data, and Tracking
articles.summary: A study of 281 popular free Android VPNs revealed widespread security failures, including traffic leaks and unencrypted data, affecting over 2.4 billion installations. The researchers found that these apps fail to provide the fundamental privacy and security protections expected by users.

articles.title: Hackers Use Fake Microsoft Entra Passkey Enrollment to Gain Microsoft 365 Access
articles.summary: Threat actor O-UNC-066 is using voice-based phishing to trick Microsoft 365 users into enrolling a malicious Entra passkey to facilitate data extortion. The attackers leverage a specialized phishing kit to intercept and control the enrollment process.

articles.title: 222 GitHub Repositories Linked to Fake Go Package Malware Operation
articles.summary: Researchers identified a network of 222 malicious GitHub repositories distributing various threats, including stealers and cryptominers, hidden within fake Go programming packages.

articles.title: FastNetMon Launches Netomics, a Self-Hosted Routing Intelligence Platform
articles.summary: FastNetMon has introduced Netomics, a new self-hosted platform designed to provide organizations with advanced routing intelligence and network visibility. The release aims to enhance infrastructure monitoring capabilities for security and network operations teams.

articles.title: Former Ransomware Negotiator Sentenced to 70 Months in Prison for Secretly Helping BlackCat Gang
articles.summary: A former ransomware negotiator has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for betraying clients by colluding with the BlackCat ransomware gang. He used confidential information gained during negotiations to assist the threat actors in their extortion schemes.

articles.title: Scot NHS Trust probes email stuffup involving maternity patients' data
articles.summary: NHS Forth Valley is investigating a data leak caused by a failure to follow basic email data protection protocols involving maternity patient information. The incident highlights a significant lapse in internal cybersecurity hygiene within the health board.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit 'Ill Bloom' Vulnerability to Drain $3.1 Million From Cryptocurrency Wallets
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting a vulnerability dubbed 'Ill Bloom,' which stems from weak randomness in cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrase generation, resulting in $3.1 million in stolen assets. Security firm Coinspect identified the flaw, which allows attackers to derive private keys and drain funds from affected wallets.

articles.title: GigaWiper Merges Three Malware Families Into One Destructive Backdoor
articles.summary: Microsoft discovered GigaWiper, a sophisticated modular Go-based backdoor that integrates espionage, remote control, and data-wiping capabilities by combining three distinct malware families. This threat was identified during investigations into destructive wiping activities within compromised enterprise environments.

articles.title: Ransomware Negotiator Gets 70 Months in Prison for Aiding BlackCat Attacks
articles.summary: A former ransomware negotiator has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for conspiring with the BlackCat ransomware group to extort victims and facilitating further cyberattacks. This case highlights legal consequences for individuals who assist ransomware operators in their illicit activities.

articles.title: July 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Is CVE tracking still practical?
articles.summary: The article discusses the unsustainable surge in Microsoft CVE releases, noting record-breaking vulnerability counts in June and questioning the long-term practicality of traditional CVE tracking.

articles.title: Workato expands Agent Studio with Headless API, AI guardrails
articles.summary: Workato has updated its Agent Studio with Headless API and Agent Guardrails, allowing AI agents to be embedded across business applications while enforcing data privacy, security, and compliance. These additions focus on secure deployment and identity-based governance for enterprise AI.

articles.title: The open source library holding up your stack might have one maintainer
articles.summary: The reliance of modern software stacks on open-source libraries maintained by individuals creates significant security risks due to potential lack of support and oversight. A new research paper highlights how these vulnerabilities are obscured by the generic 'open source' label.

articles.title: Most data brokers won’t tell you what happened to your deletion request
articles.summary: A UC Irvine study reveals that most data brokers fail to confirm whether they have processed consumer requests to delete or stop sharing personal information, undermining privacy rights provided by California law.

articles.title: Microsoft is rewriting Windows patch guidance because of AI
articles.summary: Microsoft is urging organizations to shorten their Windows patch deployment timelines, citing that AI-driven exploitation is significantly reducing the window of opportunity for defenders. The company recommends reevaluating update policies to ensure critical security fixes are applied faster to mitigate emerging threats.

articles.title: Turning software supply chain security into a daily habit
articles.summary: Anastasia Tikhonova of Group-IB discusses moving beyond static SBOM compliance to operationalizing supply chain security as a daily practice for vulnerability management and incident response. The analysis emphasizes how modern attacks leverage inherited trust to connect phishing, ransomware, and data breaches.

articles.title: AWS gives its ERP agent deny-by-default rules and a separate identity
articles.summary: AWS has enhanced its ERP automation agent by implementing deny-by-default security policies and a dedicated identity architecture to better protect sensitive financial data. These updates aim to secure automated processes like invoice matching and intercompany reconciliations within enterprise resource planning systems.

articles.title: Microsoft warns customers AI will mean busier Patch Tuesdays
articles.summary: Microsoft anticipates that the integration of AI in software development will lead to a higher volume of software vulnerabilities, resulting in more frequent or complex updates on Patch Tuesdays. Consequently, the company is positioning its automated patching tools as a necessary solution for organizations to manage the increased workload.

articles.title: Former DigitalMint ransomware negotiator who duped clients sentenced to 70 months in jail
articles.summary: Former DigitalMint employee Angelo Martino was sentenced to 70 months in prison for leaking confidential information to ransomware actors to extort $75.3 million from clients. He abused his position as a negotiator to facilitate the criminal schemes of his co-conspirators.

articles.title: Dutch police trace Odido telco cyberattack to suspected local accomplice
articles.summary: Dutch police have identified a suspected local accomplice involved in the earlier cyberattack on telecommunications provider Odido, which resulted in a data breach affecting over 6 million customers.

articles.title: An unnamed US county – perhaps in Ohio – paid $1M extortion demand to cybercriminals
articles.summary: An unidentified US county, potentially in Ohio, reportedly paid a $1 million ransom to cybercriminals following a security incident. The payment details emerged through leaked negotiation transcripts.

articles.title: INTERPOL Operation First Light Nets 5,811 Arrests and Seizes $293 Million
articles.summary: INTERPOL's Operation First Light 2026 successfully concluded with 5,811 arrests and the seizure of $293 million in illicit assets across 97 countries. The operation focused on dismantling large-scale global fraud and money laundering networks.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of GigaWiper Backdoor Built to Destroy Windows PCs
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified GigaWiper, a sophisticated Windows backdoor capable of remote access, file encryption, and complete disk destruction. This tool poses a severe threat to global systems by combining espionage capabilities with destructive data-wiping functionality.

articles.title: Dormant GitHub Accounts Help Attackers Blend In While Mapping Corporate Orgs
articles.summary: Attackers are utilizing long-dormant 'ghost' GitHub accounts and compromised tokens to scrape corporate repository data and map organizational structures. This technique allows malicious actors to evade detection by blending in with legitimate activity through automated API queries.

articles.title: GodDamn Ransomware Uses PoisonX to Blind Security Software
articles.summary: The newly identified GodDamn ransomware, a successor to the Beast family, utilizes a signed driver called PoisonX to effectively disable security software and evade detection. First appearing in May 2026, the malware demonstrates an advanced approach to neutralizing host-based defenses during attacks.

articles.title: New GigaWiper Windows Backdoor Bundles Disk Wiping, Fake Ransomware, and Spyware
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified GigaWiper, a new modular Windows backdoor that combines disk-wiping capabilities, destructive fake ransomware, and spyware into a single malicious toolkit. The malware allows attackers to choose from multiple destructive methods to permanently compromise target systems.

articles.title: Interpol cybercrime crackdown nets 5,800 arrests across 97 countries
articles.summary: Interpol's Operation First Light successfully coordinated a global anti-fraud initiative resulting in 5,800 arrests across 97 countries. The operation aimed to dismantle international social-engineering scam networks that targeted over 142,000 victims.

articles.title: AI Gateway Connected to Amazon Bedrock Hijacked for Cryptomining
articles.summary: An AI gateway using LiteLLM and Amazon Bedrock was compromised by attackers who leveraged exposed SSH activity to conduct cryptomining operations. The incident highlights the risks of misconfigured infrastructure when integrating AI-driven service gateways.

articles.title: npm 12 Disables Install Scripts by Default to Reduce Supply Chain Risk
articles.summary: npm version 12 improves supply chain security by disabling automatic execution of install scripts by default and deprecating tokens that bypass two-factor authentication. These changes require users to explicitly opt-in to previously automatic behaviors to reduce the risk of malicious package execution.

articles.title: EU 'Chat Control' snoopfest returns after vote to kill it falls short
articles.summary: The European Union's controversial 'Chat Control' proposal remains active as opponents failed to secure the necessary parliamentary majority to block the extension of interim CSAM-scanning regulations. The decision continues the debate over the balance between child protection initiatives and individual privacy rights.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: Cloud Bucket Hijacking, Windows LPE Chain, Global Fraud Bust + 17 More Stories
articles.summary: This edition of ThreatsDay details a collection of minor operational security oversights, including cloud bucket hijacking and Windows privilege escalation, that lead to significant security consequences.

articles.title: 764 splinter group leader sentenced to 40 years in jail
articles.summary: Alexis Chavez, a leader within the 764 violent extremist group, was sentenced to 40 years in prison for coercing minors into self-harm and the production of child sexual abuse material.

articles.title: Extortion crew hijacks Microsoft 365 accounts via fake passkey setup
articles.summary: The Pink cyber extortion group is compromising Microsoft 365 accounts by using vishing calls to trick employees into registering attacker-controlled passkeys. This social engineering tactic allows threat actors to gain unauthorized access by masquerading as IT support during the enrollment process.

articles.title: Latvian forestry company still restoring systems weeks after ransomware attack
articles.summary: The Latvian state-owned forestry company Latvijas Valsts Mezi is undergoing a weeks-long recovery process following a ransomware attack orchestrated by a foreign, financially motivated group.

articles.title: Citrix launches MCP Gateway to secure enterprise AI agents
articles.summary: Citrix has introduced the MCP Gateway and enhanced its NetScaler AI Gateway to provide secure routing, governance, and traffic monitoring for enterprise AI agents and LLMs. These updates allow organizations to manage and observe AI-related communications from a centralized platform.

articles.title: Vectogate debuts platform to secure and govern autonomous AI agents
articles.summary: Vectogate has launched an AI governance platform to provide centralized control and security for autonomous AI agents handling sensitive enterprise data. The solution aims to mitigate risks associated with the increasing adoption of autonomous digital employees within business systems.

articles.title: Microsoft closes book on Nightmare Eclipse's RoguePlanet zero-day
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a patch for a zero-day vulnerability in its Defender software, known as RoguePlanet, which was disclosed by the group Nightmare Eclipse several weeks ago.

articles.title: NSA revives 'Tailored Access Operations' name for elite hacking unit
articles.summary: The NSA has officially rebranded its Office of Computer Network Operations back to the historical name Tailored Access Operations. This decision revives the moniker of the agency's elite unit responsible for signals intelligence and cyber exploitation activities.

articles.title: EU takes member states to court over unimplemented cybersecurity law
articles.summary: The European Commission has initiated legal action against Ireland, Spain, France, and the Netherlands for failing to transpose the NIS2 cybersecurity directive within the required timeframe. These member states are over 20 months behind schedule in implementing regulations intended to secure critical infrastructure.

articles.title: AssuranceAmerica Breach Exposes 7 Million Driver’s Licenses After Employee Account Hack
articles.summary: AssuranceAmerica suffered a major data breach after hackers compromised an employee account, exposing the driver's license information of nearly 7 million individuals. This incident marks one of the most significant thefts of sensitive personal identification data recorded in 2026.

articles.title: AI Attacks Move in Minutes. Join This Webinar on Building a Defense That Keeps Up
articles.summary: AI-driven automation is drastically accelerating the speed of cyberattacks, allowing adversaries to execute complex campaigns in minutes rather than days. This shift necessitates a move away from human-speed defense tools to more agile, AI-based security frameworks.

articles.title: Microsoft releases fix for RoguePlanet Defender flaw (CVE-2026-50656)
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a security update to address CVE-2026-50656, a local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Malware Protection Engine that could allow attackers to gain SYSTEM-level access on Windows 10 and 11. The flaw, exploited via the RoguePlanet method, stems from improper link resolution before file access.

articles.title: GhostApproval Flaws Let Top AI Coding Tools Write Outside Workspaces
articles.summary: Wiz researchers discovered 'GhostApproval' symlink vulnerabilities in popular AI coding assistants that allow attackers to bypass security checks and gain unauthorized system access. These flaws enable AI tools to manipulate sensitive files outside of designated project workspaces.

articles.title: 5,811 arrests, $293 million seized over social engineering scams
articles.summary: Operation First Light 2026, a global law enforcement initiative involving 97 countries, resulted in 5,811 arrests and the seizure of $293 million related to international social engineering and money laundering scams.

articles.title: Summer of Clearinghouses
articles.summary: The industry is seeing a surge in cybersecurity clearinghouse announcements, including the launch of Athena, a platform focused on operationalized vulnerability remediation.

articles.title: Your coding agent says no in chat and yes in the code
articles.summary: Research from the Alan Turing Institute reveals that AI coding agents like GitHub Copilot can bypass safety filters by executing harmful code even when they refuse to generate it in chat interactions. The findings suggest that current chatbot-focused safety testing is insufficient for autonomous coding assistants capable of multi-turn file editing and script execution.

articles.title: GodDamn Ransomware Uses PoisonX Driver to Disable Endpoint Defenses
articles.summary: The newly identified GodDamn ransomware, believed to be a rebrand of Beast ransomware, utilizes the PoisonX kernel driver to bypass and disable endpoint security protections. The threat was first observed in the wild in May 2026.

articles.title: Microsoft fixed Defender flaw RoguePlanet (CVE-2026-50656)
articles.summary: Microsoft patched a high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-50656, in the Malware Protection Engine that could allow local attackers to escalate privileges via Microsoft Defender.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches RoguePlanet Defender Flaw That Can Grant SYSTEM Privileges
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a patch for the RoguePlanet vulnerability (CVE-2026-50656), a high-severity privilege escalation flaw in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine that could allow attackers to gain SYSTEM-level access.

articles.title: AWS centralizes access, spending, and governance for Claude
articles.summary: AWS has introduced a self-hosted 'Claude apps gateway' to centralize access control, cost management, and security governance for Claude Code and Desktop applications. This architecture replaces individual developer credentials with a unified control plane to improve security posture and policy enforcement.

articles.title: Fake VPN and 7-Zip Apps Turn Victims Into Residential Proxy Nodes
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are distributing trojanized versions of popular software like 7-Zip and WireVPN to compromise victim devices and convert them into residential proxy nodes. This allows attackers to route malicious traffic through innocent users' IP addresses to evade detection.

articles.title: NetSPI pairs AI pentesting with expert-validated security findings
articles.summary: NetSPI has expanded its AI-powered continuous penetration testing platform to include new services like continuous web, internal, and AI-focused testing. These services incorporate human validation to ensure accuracy in identifying and addressing evolving security threats.

articles.title: Meta's New AI Image Tool Lets Others Use Your Public Instagram Photos in AI Images
articles.summary: Meta has enabled a feature by default that allows users to incorporate public Instagram content into AI-generated images using its Muse model. This move has raised significant privacy concerns regarding the unauthorized use of personal data for generative AI training and content creation.

articles.title: Thief posed as Wi-Fi fixing hero, then stole priceless trophy
articles.summary: A thief successfully stole a priceless trophy by impersonating a technician hired to fix the Wi-Fi. The incident highlights the effectiveness of social engineering tactics in gaining unauthorized physical access.

articles.title: Malicious AI agent skills can slip past the scanners built to stop them
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified that malicious AI agent skills, distributed through public marketplaces, can bypass existing security scanning tools. These plug-and-play extensions pose a significant risk to developers using AI-driven coding environments.

articles.title: The fake report message that ends with a stolen Reddit account
articles.summary: Attackers are using social engineering on platforms like Reddit and Discord to trick users into providing login or verification codes to hijack their accounts. The scheme relies on deceptive messaging without the use of malware or malicious links.

articles.title: Top AI Agents Built to Catch Malicious Code Can Be Tricked Into Running It
articles.summary: AI coding agents designed for security analysis can be manipulated via an attack dubbed 'Friendly Fire' to execute malicious code on host machines. This vulnerability exploits the autonomous execution modes of tools like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.

articles.title: Open-source collaboration is growing worldwide and putting pressure on maintainers
articles.summary: Global cross-border open-source collaboration is accelerating at near-record rates, significantly increasing the workload and pressure on project maintainers. This surge in international contributions highlights the vital role of open-source ecosystems in the global digital economy.

articles.title: Product showcase: Protect your iPhone with McAfee Mobile Security
articles.summary: McAfee has released a mobile security application for iOS and Android that provides integrated features like scam protection, VPN services, and Wi-Fi security. The app includes a Smart Scan tool to audit device configurations and network safety.

articles.title: Wireshark 4.6.7 patches a dozen security flaws
articles.summary: Wireshark has released version 4.6.7 to address twelve security vulnerabilities, primarily involving crashes triggered by malformed packets or capture files. Users are advised to update to mitigate the risk of exploitation through untrusted data.

articles.title: GhostApproval Symlink Flaws Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code in AI Coding Agents
articles.summary: A vulnerability dubbed GhostApproval allows malicious code projects to exploit symlinks in popular AI coding assistants, enabling unauthorized write access to sensitive files on a developer's machine. This flaw affects several major AI coding tools, including Amazon Q Developer, Cursor, and Anthropic's Claude Code.

articles.title: Fake 7-Zip Installers Turn Devices Into Residential Proxy Nodes
articles.summary: A threat actor identified as Lurking Lizard is using malicious fake 7-Zip installers hosted on over 230 lookalike domains to compromise devices and turn them into nodes for a residential proxy network. The operation, which has been active since at least 2022, leverages deceptive branding to facilitate unauthorized network traffic routing.

articles.title: Iris Recognition vs Fingerprint: Which Biometric Wins in 2026?
articles.summary: This article evaluates the performance, security, and privacy implications of iris recognition versus fingerprint biometrics in the context of 2026 technological standards.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese snoops caught breaking into universities' Roundcube mailservers
articles.summary: Suspected Chinese state-sponsored actors are exploiting vulnerabilities in Roundcube mail servers to target academic institutions. Researchers estimate that the campaign has impacted several dozen individual targets.

articles.title: Ubiquiti Patches Critical UniFi OS Flaws Allowing Command Injection and Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: Ubiquiti has released security updates to address seven critical vulnerabilities in UniFi OS, most notably a maximum-severity command injection flaw tracked as CVE-2026-50746. This critical vulnerability, which carries a CVSS score of 10.0, affects the UniFi Connect Application and could allow unauthorized command execution and privilege escalation.

articles.title: Greek victims file lawsuit against Intellexa over Predator spyware
articles.summary: Greek victims have filed a lawsuit against Intellexa regarding the unauthorized use of Predator spyware, which previously triggered a major political scandal in 2022. The case highlights ongoing accountability efforts following the discovery of the spyware on numerous devices.

articles.title: Cash App owner to pay $45 million to settle allegations of lax security
articles.summary: Block, Inc. has agreed to a $45 million settlement with state attorneys general following allegations that it misled users regarding the security protections provided by Cash App. The case centered on claims that the platform failed to maintain adequate security standards and misrepresented its safety protocols.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot: Sorry Dave, I can't do that harmful thing - unless you ask me in code
articles.summary: Researchers discovered an AI jailbreak vulnerability in GitHub Copilot that allows users to bypass safety filters by embedding malicious requests within code contexts. This flaw highlights persistent security challenges in regulating generative AI workflows.

articles.title: A Hacker Claims 35 GB of Accenture Source Code. The Company discloses the data breach
articles.summary: Accenture has confirmed a significant data breach after a threat actor claimed to have stolen and offered for sale 35 GB of the company's source code, encryption keys, and Azure credentials. The stolen data reportedly includes sensitive internal information obtained during an incident in July.

articles.title: DuckDuckGo Now Blocks Most YouTube Ads Right Inside Its Browser
articles.summary: DuckDuckGo has updated its browser to include native ad-blocking capabilities for YouTube, providing users with a more streamlined and private viewing experience. This feature is now available by default across supported platforms with specific functional limitations.

articles.title: French nonprofit starts global intelligence and research hub for AI cyber threats
articles.summary: A French nonprofit has launched a global intelligence hub designed to coordinate rapid international responses to AI-driven cyber threats among governments, businesses, and experts.

articles.title: AI Coding Agents Found Triggering Endpoint Security Rules Built to Catch Attackers
articles.summary: AI coding agents like Cursor and Claude Code are inadvertently triggering endpoint security alerts by performing behavioral patterns that mimic common malicious activities, such as credential access. Security teams must differentiate these benign automated processes from actual threats to avoid alert fatigue.

articles.title: Taiwan charges two businessmen over alleged role in Chinese espionage campaign
articles.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors have charged two businessmen for allegedly facilitating a Chinese espionage operation by leasing LINE messaging accounts to foreign intelligence agents. The scheme highlights a tactical effort by state-sponsored actors to bypass security measures via compromised commercial communication platforms.

articles.title: New HalluSquatting Attack Could Trick AI Coding Assistants Into Installing Botnet Malware
articles.summary: Researchers discovered 'HalluSquatting,' a technique where attackers register non-existent package names recommended by AI coding assistants to trick developers into downloading malicious botnet code. This exploits the tendency of AI models to hallucinate software libraries, turning those fabrications into a supply chain attack vector.

articles.title: Ubiquiti Patches Critical UniFi Flaws Across Connect, Talk, Access, Protect, and OS
articles.summary: Ubiquiti has released critical security patches for multiple UniFi applications and OS components to address vulnerabilities that could allow for privilege escalation and arbitrary command execution. A notable flaw, CVE-2026-50746, carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 due to improper access controls.

articles.title: Armored Likho Hits Government, Energy Sectors With BusySnake Stealer
articles.summary: The Armored Likho APT group is targeting government and energy sectors using AI-generated loaders and the BusySnake information stealer. The campaign relies on sophisticated phishing tactics to compromise sensitive infrastructure.

articles.title: Former UK privacy chief preparing legal action against woman who reported him, minister says
articles.summary: The UK's Science Secretary expressed outrage after an investigation confirmed sexual harassment and bullying at the Information Commissioner’s Office, where the former chief is now pursuing legal action against his accuser.

articles.title: Attackers using Langflow flaw for credential harvesting (CVE-2026-55255)
articles.summary: CISA has added the Langflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-55255) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of attackers using the flaw for credential harvesting. The security hole affects the open-source visual framework used for building AI agents and workflows.

articles.title: Bug in top AI coding agents shows that Unix-era security headaches never really die
articles.summary: A vulnerability dubbed 'GhostApproval' in AI coding agents exposes critical weaknesses in human-in-the-loop workflows, mirroring historical Unix security flaws. This issue allows unauthorized code changes to bypass human verification processes, potentially leading to supply chain compromise.

articles.title: China tells devs to ditch Claude Code over 'backdoor code' fears
articles.summary: Chinese authorities have advised developers to stop using Claude Code, citing concerns that its internal monitoring mechanisms could potentially exfiltrate user data to remote servers.

articles.title: Censys Internet Map links real-time DNS data to internet infrastructure
articles.summary: Censys has updated its Internet Map platform to integrate real-time DNS data, allowing security teams to centralize infrastructure investigation within a single interface. This enhancement enables seamless pivoting between domains, DNS records, and underlying IP infrastructure.

articles.title: Spain arrests alleged supporter of pro-Russian hacktivist groups after FBI tip
articles.summary: Spanish authorities arrested a man linked to pro-Russian hacktivist groups CyberArmy of Russia Reborn, Z-Pentest, and NoName057(16) following an investigation assisted by the FBI.

articles.title: Blackpoint AI SOC Agent autonomously contains identity-based attacks
articles.summary: Blackpoint Cyber has launched an AI-powered SOC agent designed to autonomously detect and contain identity-based attacks against Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace within seconds. This tool utilizes a hybrid AI and human approach to mitigate credential-based threats faster than traditional manual response methods.

articles.title: First Recon AI Security Runtime helps enterprises govern AI with audit-ready evidence
articles.summary: First Recon AI has launched its AI Security Runtime, a platform designed to govern and secure enterprise AI interactions while providing audit-ready evidence for compliance. It enables organizations to monitor human-to-model and agent-to-agent communications to enforce security policies in real-time.

articles.title: FalconStor Cloud Clean Room enables validated recovery without dedicated infrastructure
articles.summary: FalconStor has launched a cloud-based 'Clean Room' platform that utilizes zero-trust secure enclave technology to facilitate validated, isolated recovery testing without requiring dedicated physical infrastructure.

articles.title: EU unveils cyber plan to reduce reliance on foreign AI systems
articles.summary: The European Union has introduced a new cybersecurity strategy aimed at reducing dependency on foreign artificial intelligence by fostering domestic development and ensuring regional security. The plan focuses on enhancing the safety and accessibility of frontier AI technologies within the EU cyber ecosystem.

articles.title: OpenMatter Network Joins HOL Initiative to Help Define Standards for Verifiable AI Collaboration and Security
articles.summary: OpenMatter Network has partnered with the HOL Initiative to establish industry-wide standards for secure and verifiable AI collaboration. This initiative aims to address safety and security challenges in interconnected artificial intelligence systems.

articles.title: New Ghost Phishing Wave Is Breaking Traditional Email Security
articles.summary: A sophisticated 'ghost phishing' campaign known as EvilTokens is bypassing traditional email security by obfuscating malicious content until it executes within the victim's browser. This technique poses a significant risk to organizations by potentially compromising Microsoft 365 credentials and sensitive data.

articles.title: SCMBANKER Malware Uses ClickFix Lures to Target Mexican Banking Users
articles.summary: A threat actor tracked as REF6045 is deploying SCMBANKER malware against Mexican financial and crypto institutions using fake CAPTCHA 'ClickFix' lures. The attack tricks users into executing a malicious PowerShell script to compromise their systems.

articles.title: DNSFilter makes its DNS threat protection available to OEM partners
articles.summary: DNSFilter has launched an OEM program allowing ISPs, device manufacturers, and security firms to integrate its protective DNS, domain analysis, and VPN/firewall solutions into their own platforms. This move aims to broaden the reach of their threat-blocking capabilities through third-party product bundling.

articles.title: Attestiv DeepScan combines AI and forensic analysis for file validation
articles.summary: Attestiv has launched DeepScan, an AI-powered platform designed to automatically validate the authenticity of files like photos, documents, and media within business workflows. The tool integrates forensic analysis to help organizations verify trust in customer-submitted content and combat deepfake threats.

articles.title: UNK_MassTraction Exploits Roundcube Flaws Against US, Canadian Universities
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor UNK_MassTraction is exploiting vulnerabilities in Roundcube webmail to compromise research email servers at universities in the U.S. and Canada. The attackers are successfully stealing user sessions to gain unauthorized access to sensitive academic data.

articles.title: GitHub 'Verified' Commits Can Be Rewritten Into New Hashes Without Breaking Signatures
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that Git commit hashes can be rewritten while maintaining a valid signature, allowing attackers to create deceptive commits that GitHub erroneously marks as 'Verified'. This vulnerability undermines the integrity of code review processes by allowing for the generation of valid-looking but technically distinct commits.

articles.title: The Verification Step Is the New ATO Battleground in 2026
articles.summary: As traditional credential stuffing becomes less effective due to the adoption of passkeys, attackers are shifting their focus to exploiting the identity verification process to facilitate account takeovers.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot Refuses Harmful Requests in Chat, Then Writes Them in Code
articles.summary: Researchers found that AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot can be manipulated into generating malicious code by breaking dangerous requests into smaller, innocuous steps within the code editor. This highlights a security bypass vulnerability in current LLM-based development tools.

articles.title: Telegram-Hosted RedWing Malware Lets Anyone Rent Android Spyware Tools
articles.summary: The RedWing Android banking trojan is being distributed as a subscription-based malware-as-a-service model via Telegram, showing potential ties to the Oblivion malware family and Russian threat actors. It lowers the barrier to entry for cybercriminals by providing comprehensive tutorials and documentation for its spyware capabilities.

articles.title: Crusoe brings serverless fine-tuning to AI model development
articles.summary: Crusoe has introduced serverless fine-tuning and self-serve deployment capabilities to its Intelligence Foundry platform, streamlining the development and production of custom AI models. These tools aim to reduce infrastructure management overhead for data scientists and ML engineers working with open-weight models.

articles.title: Automox MCP Server adds visual reviews and AI-driven patch policy creation
articles.summary: Automox has released version 2.2 of its MCP Server, introducing interactive visual review tools and AI-powered patch policy creation to enhance governance in endpoint operations. This update aims to move beyond simple natural-language interaction by providing IT teams with better oversight and actionable context for automated patch management.

articles.title: China-Linked UAT-7810 Expands ORB Network With New LONGLEASH Malware
articles.summary: Chinese threat actor UAT-7810 is expanding its LapDogs ORB network by compromising internet-facing devices with new bespoke malware named LONGLEASH. This activity highlights the ongoing development of advanced infrastructure by persistent actors.

articles.title: Thousands of malicious AI skills found capable of stealing data, running malware
articles.summary: The ESET H1 2026 Threat Report identified over 25,000 suspicious AI skills capable of stealing user data and executing malware. These malicious extensions significantly expand the attack surface for AI agents by abusing their permissions to perform unauthorized tasks.

articles.title: Found fast, fixed slow: The gap the AI clearinghouse must close
articles.summary: The government's AI clearinghouse needs to prioritize rapid vulnerability remediation over mere discovery to be effective. Relying solely on scanning without integrated patching processes risks rendering the initiative ineffective.

articles.title: ScienceLogic adds geographic service visibility to Skylar One
articles.summary: ScienceLogic has released the 'Kyoto' update for its Skylar One observability platform, introducing new features for geographic service visibility and improved hybrid IT infrastructure management. This update focuses on enhancing AI workload monitoring and platform scalability for enterprise environments.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Adobe ColdFusion, Joomlack Page Builder, Langflow, and JoomShaper SP Page Builder flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include multiple security flaws found in Adobe ColdFusion, Joomlack Page Builder, Langflow, and JoomShaper SP Page Builder. Federal agencies are mandated to remediate these specific vulnerabilities to mitigate active exploitation risks.

articles.title: Codenotary launches AI security platform that learns from AI agent behavior
articles.summary: Codenotary has launched AgentMon 3, an AI security platform that utilizes adaptive runtime policies to monitor and learn from AI agent behavior within organizational workflows. The tool is now available on the AWS Marketplace to simplify enterprise deployment.

articles.title: CISA Deploys Anthropic’s Mythos AI to Hunt Vulnerabilities in U.S. Government Code
articles.summary: CISA has begun utilizing Anthropic’s Mythos AI to proactively scan federal government code repositories for security vulnerabilities. This initiative aims to identify and remediate potential flaws before they can be exploited by foreign intelligence services or cybercriminals.

articles.title: Claude Cowork turns your phone into a remote control for AI work
articles.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Cowork, an AI agent capable of executing multi-step tasks across various applications that persist in the background even when devices are offline. This tool allows users to manage complex workflows remotely through mobile and web interfaces.

articles.title: 15-Year-Old GhostLock Flaw Enables Root and Container Escape on Most Linux Distros
articles.summary: GhostLock (CVE-2026-43499) is a 15-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unprivileged local users to gain root access and escape containers. The flaw affects nearly all mainstream distributions since 2011 and requires immediate patching.

articles.title: Orbia CISO Miranda Ritchie on building security into sustainable infrastructure
articles.summary: Orbia CISO Miranda Ritchie discusses the critical intersection of cybersecurity, safety, and sustainable infrastructure within industrial control systems. She emphasizes embedding security into project lifecycles to mitigate risks to personnel and the environment caused by legacy hardware and distributed operational technology.

articles.title: CISA Adds 4 Actively Exploited Adobe, Joomla, and Langflow Flaws to KEV
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include four actively exploited security flaws discovered in Adobe ColdFusion, Joomla, and Langflow. These additions require federal agencies to remediate the vulnerabilities within a specified timeframe to mitigate active threats.

articles.title: 20 open-source cybersecurity tools to keep your team ready for anything
articles.summary: This article highlights 20 open-source cybersecurity tools designed to assist security teams with vulnerability research, application testing, and AI-specific infrastructure protection. It emphasizes the growing need for tools that secure AI systems against emerging threats like exposed endpoints.

articles.title: macOS is becoming a proving ground for AI agents
articles.summary: The emergence of AI agents capable of autonomous operation on macOS systems presents new security challenges regarding automated workflows and potential threat actor abuse. These agents simulate human interaction, which could be exploited to perform unauthorized tasks or automate malicious processes.

articles.title: How to implement a continuous offensive security testing program
articles.summary: This article discusses the shift from static penetration testing to continuous offensive security programs, addressing the need for constant monitoring to keep pace with evolving network environments and emerging threats.

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic are pulling in different directions
articles.summary: The increasing use of autonomous AI agents in operational workflows creates a potential security gap due to unpredictable behavioral drift that eludes traditional monitoring. An analysis of hiring trends at OpenAI and Anthropic suggests that these companies are prioritizing different developmental paths for agentic AI.

articles.title: Why Unity Remains the Most Popular Engine for Mobile Games
articles.summary: This article discusses the technical advantages and industry-standard features that make the Unity game engine a preferred choice for mobile game development. It focuses on development efficiency and scalability rather than security risks.

articles.title: Vidar Stealer Unmasked: Code Signing Abuse, Go Loaders and File Inflation
articles.summary: The Vidar Stealer campaign employs advanced evasion techniques, including code signing abuse and a custom Go-based loader that utilizes DLL sideloading to infect systems. This combination of a loader-as-a-service framework and file inflation represents a sophisticated evolution in threat actor methodology.

articles.title: Spain arrests suspected hacker linked to Russian hacktivist campaign
articles.summary: Spanish authorities have arrested a suspected hacker allegedly involved in cyberattacks orchestrated by the Russian hacktivist groups Cyber Army of Russia Reborn and NoName. The individual is currently being investigated for their role in these hostile campaigns.

articles.title: Critical Gitea Docker Bug Under Active Exploitation Exposes Repositories and Secrets
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20896) in Gitea Docker images that allows unauthorized access to sensitive repositories and secrets. Users are urged to upgrade to version 1.26.3 or later to remediate the flaw.

articles.title: Windows is watching: Anti-piracy tool fingers Scattered Spider suspect
articles.summary: Microsoft's Windows GDID telemetry tool has been utilized to identify a suspect associated with the Scattered Spider cybercriminal group. This case highlights how pervasive OS-level tracking can be leveraged by law enforcement to trace malicious online activity.

articles.title: Deepfake CSAM lawsuit against xAI, Grok expands
articles.summary: A lawsuit involving the generation of non-consensual deepfake sexual images of minors using xAI's Grok and Stability AI has expanded to include additional victims and defendants. The case highlights the legal and ethical challenges surrounding generative AI tools and child safety.

articles.title: GitHub AI agent leaks private repos when asked nicely
articles.summary: A security vulnerability nicknamed GitLost in a GitHub AI agent allows unauthorized users to access private repositories through simple prompt injection techniques. Currently, there is no official fix or documentation addressing the exploit.

articles.title: Spanish Police Arrest Man Linked to CARR, Z-Pentest, and NoName057(16)
articles.summary: Spanish police, in collaboration with the FBI, arrested a suspect in Palencia for providing coordination and financial support to pro-Russian hacking groups including CARR, Z-Pentest, and NoName057(16). The individual faces charges related to terrorism and cyberattacks.

articles.title: CAI cloud worm gives competitors' malware the boot, then steals secrets and mines for coin
articles.summary: A new cloud-based worm dubbed CAI is infecting environments not only to steal credentials and mine cryptocurrency but also to actively remove competing malware from the compromised systems. This behavior highlights an emerging trend of malicious actors sabotaging one another to maximize their control over infected infrastructure.

articles.title: RedWing MaaS Packages Android Bank Fraud as a Telegram Rental Service
articles.summary: The RedWing Android banking malware is being distributed as a Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) subscription on Telegram, enabling low-skill threat actors to steal banking credentials and intercept 2FA codes. Researchers believe this operation is a new variant of the previously identified Oblivion malware.

articles.title: 7 Arrested Over World’s Top Anime Piracy Site HiAnime
articles.summary: Vietnamese authorities, in collaboration with US law enforcement and the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment, arrested seven individuals linked to the operation of the major anime piracy platform HiAnime, which generated $12.85 million in advertising revenue.

articles.title: Rogue Agent Flaw Could Have Let Attackers Hijack Google Dialogflow CX Chatbots
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in Google Dialogflow CX allowed attackers with restricted access to hijack other chatbots within the same cloud project. This flaw enabled unauthorized access to sensitive user data and the ability to manipulate chatbot responses for phishing purposes.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows Texas app law requiring age verification to take effect
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has permitted the Texas App Store Accountability Act to take effect, allowing the state to enforce age verification requirements on app stores. This decision denies an emergency request to stay the law while ongoing legal challenges proceed in lower courts.

articles.title: Predatorgate snoopfest victims launch €8M sueball at spyware maker
articles.summary: Victims of the 'Predator' spyware have initiated an €8 million lawsuit against the spyware developer in Greece. This legal action coincides with increased pressure from human rights organizations for the EU to implement stricter regulations against spyware abuse.

articles.title: Britain plans to build autonomous AI 'Cyber Shield' to defend nation
articles.summary: The British government is developing an autonomous 'Cyber Shield' to combat large-scale, machine-speed cyber threats identified by the National Cyber Security Centre. This initiative aims to enhance national defense by enabling automated detection and rapid response to sophisticated digital attacks.

articles.title: DEBULL Tooling Abuses Microsoft Device-Code Flow to Target M365 Accounts
articles.summary: The DEBULL phishing campaign exploits the legitimate Microsoft 365 device-code authentication flow by using social engineering lures to hijack user accounts. By bypassing traditional fake login pages, attackers trick victims into authorizing malicious device access directly through Microsoft's own interface.

articles.title: Major Japanese telco says cyberattack exposed 12 million emails
articles.summary: A major Japanese telecommunications company reported a cyberattack that exposed 12 million emails across five of its internet service providers. The breach compromised systems managing customer accounts, webmail services, and email storage.

articles.title: Public GitHub Issue Could Trick GitHub Agentic Workflows Into Leaking Private Repo Data
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a vulnerability where malicious actors can manipulate GitHub Agentic Workflows via public issues to exfiltrate data from an organization's private repositories. The attack requires no authentication or prior access, exploiting overly permissive agent configurations.

articles.title: Barracuda adds PAM and identity protection with Evo Security acquisition
articles.summary: Barracuda Networks has acquired Evo Security to integrate privileged access management and advanced identity protection capabilities into its BarracudaONE platform. This strategic move aims to provide a unified identity security architecture in response to the growing demand for comprehensive IAM solutions.

articles.title: CyberProof Agentic MXDR Service brings AI agents to managed detection and response
articles.summary: CyberProof has launched an Agentic MXDR service that utilizes AI agents to automate and integrate various security operations while maintaining human-governed oversight. The service aims to replace manual workflows in threat intelligence, hunting, and monitoring with an expert-validated AI system.

articles.title: Picus Autonomous Exposure Validation Platform validates real-world CVE exploitability
articles.summary: Picus Security has introduced an Autonomous Exposure Validation Platform designed to help organizations rapidly assess their vulnerability to real-world CVE exploits. The tool aims to bridge the gap between vulnerability disclosure and the ability to verify if security controls can effectively mitigate emerging threats.

articles.title: Court Filing Reveals Windows Device ID Helped FBI Trace Alleged Scattered Spider Hacker
articles.summary: U.S. prosecutors linked a 19-year-old alleged Scattered Spider hacker to a retail intrusion by tracking a persistent Windows device ID from Microsoft records to the suspect's accounts. The case highlights how hardware-level identifiers can be critical in deanonymizing cybercriminals.

articles.title: Writer AI Flaw Could Let Agent Previews Leak Session Tokens Across Tenants
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a critical session isolation flaw in the Writer AI platform, codenamed WriteOut, which allowed for cross-tenant unauthorized access by leaking session tokens. The vulnerability has since been patched by the vendor.

articles.title: UK cyber pledge draws only a handful of top firms despite ministerial appeal
articles.summary: A UK government initiative to boost corporate cybersecurity engagement has received low participation from major companies, despite being backed by high-profile firms like the London Stock Exchange and Marks & Spencer. The initiative follows significant recent cyber incidents that have impacted major businesses.

articles.title: GitLost: GitHub’s AI Agent Tricked Into Leaking Private Repository Data
articles.summary: Noma Labs identified a prompt injection vulnerability called GitLost that allowed unauthorized access to private GitHub repository data by exploiting the platform's AI agent and insufficient guardrails. This flaw demonstrates a significant security risk where manipulated public interactions can bypass access controls for sensitive information.

articles.title: Enterprise AI still smarting from leaping before looking
articles.summary: Enterprises are experiencing a high frequency of security incidents and vulnerabilities as a result of rapidly adopting artificial intelligence without adequate security considerations. A majority of organizations surveyed report issues directly stemming from their AI deployments.

articles.title: Commvault measures cyber recovery readiness with AI attack simulations
articles.summary: Commvault has launched 'Commvault Minutes to Recovery,' a cyber resilience simulation tool that utilizes AI to help organizations test their incident response and recovery capabilities against modern attack scenarios. The initiative highlights the critical need for rapid recovery, noting that the window for exploitation has shrunk to just 29 minutes.

articles.title: Attackers exploit critical Adobe ColdFusion vulnerability (CVE-2026-48282)
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Adobe ColdFusion (CVE-2026-48282) shortly after technical analysis was published. Honeypot sensors detected exploitation attempts just two days after Adobe released the patch.

articles.title: What Changes When Your Software Supply Chain Includes AI Writing Your Code?
articles.summary: The integration of AI into software development pipelines introduces new security complexities, shifting the traditional supply chain focus beyond open-source dependencies to include risks associated with AI-generated code.

articles.title: Fake IT bods on Microsoft Teams coax workers into installing malware
articles.summary: Attackers are impersonating IT helpdesk staff on Microsoft Teams to trick employees into granting remote access and installing the EtherRAT trojan. This social engineering campaign exploits trust to facilitate unauthorized system access and malware deployment.

articles.title: Radware updates Agentic AI Protection with AI governance and compliance capabilities
articles.summary: Radware has enhanced its Agentic AI Protection solution to include new governance, compliance reporting, and security features for enterprise AI agents. These updates aim to help organizations meet global AI standards while securing environments that utilize third-party tools like Anthropic Claude Code.

articles.title: 4 Best Email Security Solutions to Keep Employee Inboxes Safe
articles.summary: This article provides a comparative review of top email security solutions, highlighting essential features like AI-based threat detection and phishing protection for organizational use.

articles.title: Spain collars alleged pro-Russia hacktivist after FBI tip-off
articles.summary: Spanish authorities arrested a man in Palencia for his suspected involvement in several pro-Russian hacktivist groups and for assisting a Ukrainian hacker in fleeing to Russia. The operation was facilitated by a tip-off from the FBI.

articles.title: Government's cyber pledge lands 60 signatories, including M&S and, somehow, Capita
articles.summary: The UK government has secured 60 corporate signatories for a new cyber hygiene pledge, featuring major retailers and Capita despite the latter's recent history of high-profile data breaches. The initiative aims to standardize security practices across the private sector through voluntary commitments.

articles.title: Hidden Tenda Router Backdoor Grants Admin Access, No Patch Available
articles.summary: CERT/CC has issued an alert regarding an unpatched authentication backdoor in multiple Tenda router models that allows attackers to gain full administrative access. There is currently no patch available to remediate this vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-11405.

articles.title: Suspected China-Aligned Hackers Exploit Roundcube Flaws Against Universities
articles.summary: Suspected China-aligned threat actors are exploiting critical vulnerabilities in Roundcube webmail software to target U.S. and Canadian university departments. The campaign focuses on siphoning credentials by leveraging security flaws like CVE-2024-42009.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese espionage group used a Roundcube exploit chain to burrow into universities
articles.summary: A suspected Chinese espionage group is actively exploiting a chain of vulnerabilities in Roundcube webmail to target university physics and engineering departments. Researchers warn that the campaign remains ongoing and poses a significant risk to academic institutions.

articles.title: AI-Generated Malware Powers New Armored Likho APT Campaign
articles.summary: The newly identified APT group Armored Likho is targeting government and infrastructure sectors in Russia, Kazakhstan, and Brazil using AI-generated malware and the BusySnake Stealer. The campaign exhibits a dual focus on both state-sponsored espionage and financial theft.

articles.title: Januscape: 16-Year-Old Linux KVM Bug Enables Cloud VM Escape Attacks
articles.summary: A 16-year-old use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux KVM hypervisor, dubbed Januscape, allows guest virtual machines to corrupt host kernel memory and potentially perform escape attacks. The flaw impacts both Intel and AMD systems.

articles.title: CERT/CC Warns of Hidden Admin Backdoor in Tenda Router Firmware
articles.summary: CERT/CC has issued an advisory regarding an undocumented authentication backdoor in Tenda router firmware that allows attackers to bypass password verification. This vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-11405, grants unauthorized administrative access to the web management interface of affected devices.

articles.title: Researchers make the case for a cybersecurity AI scientist
articles.summary: Researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences are proposing a 'Cybersecurity AI Scientist' to automate security research, aiming to move beyond manual experimentation and address the scarcity of human expertise. This initiative seeks to apply autonomous AI agents to scientific discovery, mirroring their emerging success in practical penetration testing and vulnerability analysis.

articles.title: Review: Building Machine Learning Systems with a Feature Store
articles.summary: This article reviews Jim Dowling's book on building machine learning systems using feature stores, focusing on transitioning models from static datasets to real-time production environments. It highlights practical strategies for deploying robust, data-driven machine learning infrastructure.

articles.title: Your company already adopted AI and nobody is governing access
articles.summary: The rapid and unmonitored adoption of AI tools in the workplace is creating significant security risks, including unauthorized OAuth access and inherited permissions that lack corporate governance. CTO Antoine Berton warns that these shadow AI integrations expand the enterprise attack surface beyond current IT oversight.

articles.title: BeyondTrust Patches Critical Auth Bypass Flaws in Remote Support and PRA
articles.summary: BeyondTrust has released critical security patches for Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access to mitigate authentication bypass vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated attackers to gain control of affected devices.

articles.title: Apple Container: Open-source tool for Linux containers on the Mac
articles.summary: Apple has released an open-source tool called Container that allows developers to run Linux containers on Apple silicon Macs using individual, lightweight virtual machines. The tool is compatible with standard OCI images, enabling seamless integration with existing container registries.

articles.title: Microsoft wants to keep your AI agents from going rogue
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to provide a policy-driven security layer that restricts AI agent behavior and prevents them from performing unauthorized actions. This new tool simplifies the implementation of isolation controls for developers by enforcing runtime constraints on Windows and WSL.

articles.title: Power shortages could slow AI data center expansion
articles.summary: AI data center expansion is increasingly constrained by power shortages and infrastructure limitations, making electricity access a primary factor in project development. This operational bottleneck is impacting how quickly new AI capacity can be deployed globally.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: July 7, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security lists current job openings for cybersecurity professionals, including roles in application security and analysis for companies like Gett and Cynet Security.

articles.title: FBI and Spanish Police Arrest Alleged Cyber Army of Russia Reborn Member
articles.summary: The FBI and Spanish authorities have arrested an alleged member of the pro-Russia hacktivist group Cyber Army of Russia Reborn. This action reflects ongoing international collaboration to disrupt state-aligned cyber threat actors.

articles.title: Canadian spy agency reports hacking three criminal groups in 2025
articles.summary: Canada's Communications Security Establishment conducted offensive cyber operations against three distinct criminal organizations in 2025, including a ransomware-as-a-service gang. These actions represent a targeted disruption of illicit activities by a national intelligence agency.

articles.title: Attackers vote themselves $20 million in BONK cryptocurrency
articles.summary: Attackers exploited a governance mechanism in BonkDAO to fraudulently approve a proposal that transferred $20 million worth of BONK cryptocurrency to their wallets. This incident highlights a significant vulnerability in decentralized governance structures.

articles.title: Adobe ColdFusion flaw CVE-2026-48282 now exploited in the wild
articles.summary: A critical path traversal vulnerability in Adobe ColdFusion, tracked as CVE-2026-48282, is being actively exploited in the wild to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaw affects versions 2025.9, 2023.20, and earlier.

articles.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Use New Cavern C2 Framework to Target Israeli Organizations
articles.summary: An Iranian state-affiliated hacking group is utilizing a newly discovered modular C2 framework called Cavern to target Israeli IT and government sectors. The activity, tracked by Check Point Research, highlights evolving tactics used by the Ministry of Intelligence and Security to conduct targeted espionage.

articles.title: Major medical device manufacturer notifies nearly 4 million of breach
articles.summary: A major medical device manufacturer suffered a data breach affecting nearly 4 million individuals, resulting in the unauthorized access of sensitive data such as Social Security numbers and health information. Although the company reported no evidence of data exposure on the public internet, the incident remains a significant compromise of protected personal health information.

articles.title: US Army websites defaced with pro-Kurdish sentiments, insults to Trump
articles.summary: Two US Army websites were compromised via 404 hijacking to display pro-Kurdish messages and insults directed at the former president. The sites were subsequently taken offline by officials for investigation.

articles.title: 16-Year-Old Linux KVM Flaw Lets Guest VMs Escape to Host on Intel and AMD x86 Systems
articles.summary: A 16-year-old use-after-free vulnerability, dubbed 'Januscape' (CVE-2026-53359), in the Linux KVM hypervisor allows guest virtual machines to compromise the host kernel on Intel and AMD systems. The flaw resides in the shared shadow MMU code and is capable of causing host system panics.

articles.title: EU urged to act after Pegasus infects phone of spyware inquiry MEP
articles.summary: EU officials and campaigners are calling for immediate regulatory action following the discovery of Pegasus spyware on the device of a member of the European Parliament. The incident highlights ongoing security concerns regarding surveillance technology and underscores the need to implement recommendations from the PEGA Committee.

articles.title: Japanese teen arrested over cyberattack that disrupted anime streaming service
articles.summary: A Japanese teenager was arrested for exploiting a vulnerability in an anime streaming platform to perform unauthorized cancellations of over 46,000 user subscriptions. The incident highlights the impact of service-specific flaws on business operations and user account integrity.

articles.title: Threat Actors Probe Gitea Docker Flaw CVE-2026-20896 13 Days After Disclosure
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical Gitea Docker vulnerability, CVE-2026-20896, which allows unauthenticated attackers to gain elevated access. The exploit attempts were detected just 13 days after the vulnerability's initial disclosure.

articles.title: Sysdig clocks first documented case of agentic ransomware
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified the first documented instance of an AI-driven agentic ransomware attack, which enabled attackers to accelerate their operations and reduce the complexity of the exploit. This marks a notable evolution in how threat actors utilize autonomous AI agents to conduct malicious campaigns.

articles.title: From Image-to-3D to AI Agents: How AI 3D Generation Operates in 2026
articles.summary: This article explores the technical advancements in AI-driven 3D generation tools that convert text, images, and video into 3D models for various creative industries. It focuses on the capabilities of Meshy AI rather than cybersecurity threats.

articles.title: Criminal IP integrates threat intelligence with OpenCTI for automated indicator enrichment
articles.summary: Criminal IP has integrated its threat intelligence services with the OpenCTI platform, allowing security teams to automatically enrich and structure infrastructure data like IP addresses, domains, and URLs. This integration enables enhanced threat visualization and improved prioritization of indicators within the OpenCTI knowledge graph.

articles.title: Ukrainian media outlets now among 'priority targets' for Russian hackers
articles.summary: Ukrainian security officials report an escalation in Russian cyberattacks specifically targeting the nation's media organizations. Two previously undisclosed attacks highlight a shifting trend in which media outlets are now considered priority targets for state-sponsored threat actors.

articles.title: LTM’s BlueVerse RightLogic combines AI risk assessment with cyber remediation planning
articles.summary: LTM has introduced BlueVerse RightLogic, a cybersecurity framework that integrates AI-driven risk assessment with remediation planning to help enterprises manage exposure as they adopt new AI technologies.

articles.title: OpenSSH 10.4 arrives with security fixes and a post-quantum signature option
articles.summary: OpenSSH version 10.4 has been released, addressing eight security vulnerabilities and introducing support for post-quantum signature schemes. The update includes patches for issues discovered by the Swival Security Scanner, including a flaw in sftp.

articles.title: Hidden Web Prompts Trick AI Agents Into Sending Money
articles.summary: Researchers have identified active campaigns using indirect prompt injection to manipulate AI agents into executing unauthorized financial transactions. This vulnerability leverages hidden instructions on malicious websites to deceive autonomous workflows into trusting fake sites and initiating payments.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Proxy Botnets, Browser Ransomware, AI Agent Tricks, Fake PoC Malware and More
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity landscape highlights a surge in attacks leveraging mundane infrastructure, such as home streaming devices and untrustworthy software dependencies, to facilitate botnet and ransomware campaigns. The recurring theme is the exploitation of inherent trust in ordinary systems, ranging from browser permissions to AI agent instructions.

articles.title: ClickFix Scams Abuse Google, Cloudflare Checks to Deliver 7 Malware Families
articles.summary: Threat actors are leveraging fake Google and Cloudflare browser verification pages, known as ClickFix, to trick users into executing malicious scripts that install various malware families. This campaign utilizes a shared infrastructure to deliver at least seven types of malware, including StealC and NetSupport.

articles.title: Brit supermarket giant triples down on facial recog to nab shoplifters
articles.summary: A major British supermarket chain is expanding its use of facial recognition technology to an additional 150 stores by the end of the year to combat shoplifting. This expansion has drawn criticism regarding privacy concerns and surveillance practices.

articles.title: Insignary Closes SBOM Accuracy Gap With Binary-Level Clarity for Regulatory Risk
articles.summary: Insignary has introduced binary-level analysis technology to improve the accuracy of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) reporting, addressing key regulatory compliance requirements. This solution helps organizations identify hidden security risks within software components to ensure better adherence to industry standards.

articles.title: How to Evaluate an AI SOC Platform in 2026: 6 Capabilities That Separate Leaders from Bolt-On AI solutions
articles.summary: The article provides a framework for evaluating AI-driven Security Operations Center (SOC) platforms, distinguishing between superficial 'bolt-on' AI assistants and advanced autonomous agent platforms. It aims to help organizations select solutions that provide meaningful operational improvements over legacy SIEM-based tools.

articles.title: Suspected China-Nexus Hackers Use Fake Indian Tax Filing Utility to Deploy DcRAT
articles.summary: Suspected China-linked threat actors are targeting Indian taxpayers with spear-phishing emails containing a fake tax utility that deploys the DcRAT malware to steal sensitive data. The campaign, identified as Operation DragonReturn, specifically aims to compromise financial professionals and corporate entities.

articles.title: Moody Bible Institute breach leaves 2.3M accounts needing salvation, says cyber expert
articles.summary: Moody Bible Institute confirmed a cyberattack resulting in the leak of personal data for 2.3 million accounts, with the threat actor ShinyHunters exposing names, addresses, and dates of birth.

articles.title: AI Can Forge Documents in Minutes – “Looks Right” Is No Longer Enough
