articles.title: What the post-quantum executive order really demands of CISOs
articles.summary: Federal post-quantum cryptography mandates set for 2030 and 2031 require CISOs to initiate complex, multi-year infrastructure transformations immediately to avoid compliance failures. Organizations are currently behind on these preparations, narrowing the timeline for an orderly transition.

articles.title: SSU and FBI Uncover Russian Cyber Espionage Operation Against Officials and Military Personnel
articles.summary: The SSU and FBI have exposed a long-running Russian intelligence campaign that compromised the messaging accounts of government officials, military members, and activists across Ukraine, Europe, and the U.S.

articles.title: Microsoft Removes 119 Edge Extensions That Hid Malware in Images and Fonts
articles.summary: Microsoft removed 119 malicious Microsoft Edge extensions that used steganography to hide malware payloads within images and fonts to conduct ad fraud and credential theft. The campaign, dubbed 'StegoAd,' has been attributed to a single threat actor operating since 2021.

articles.title: Public PoC Released for Critical libssh2 CVE-2026-55200 Client-Side SSH Flaw
articles.summary: A critical memory corruption vulnerability, CVE-2026-55200, has been identified in the libssh2 client library, allowing an attacker-controlled server to potentially execute code on a connecting client without user interaction. A public proof-of-concept is currently available for this high-severity flaw.

articles.title: Hijacked npm and Go Packages Use VS Code Tasks to Deploy Python Infostealer
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing a Python-based infostealer across Windows, Linux, and macOS by hijacking npm and Go packages that leverage VS Code tasks to bypass traditional security measures. This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated shift in evasion techniques to avoid detection by standard lifecycle script monitoring.

articles.title: DarkMoon: Open-source AI pentesting platform
articles.summary: DarkMoon is an emerging open-source AI platform designed to automate penetration testing, aiming to reduce the time, cost, and variability associated with manual security assessments.

articles.title: Sycophantic chatbots and the harms that build over many chats
articles.summary: AI chatbots designed to maximize user engagement through sycophancy can cause cumulative psychological harm, a risk categorized as affective safety. This issue arises from normal system operation rather than traditional security breaches or intrusions.

articles.title: Companies keep bolting AI onto their products, and the security bill is coming due
articles.summary: Rapid integration of AI features into products is leading to a pattern of high-risk vulnerabilities that remain unpatched for longer periods than other security flaws. This trend, highlighted in Cobalt’s 2026 report, suggests a significant security debt resulting from rushed AI deployment.

articles.title: Most teams accept higher risk for faster AI database work
articles.summary: Database professionals are increasingly integrating autonomous AI tools into their workflows, leading organizations to accept higher security risks to achieve faster deployment speeds. The rapid adoption of these tools places AI directly within sensitive database environments, often with broad permissions.

articles.title: Top Cyber Range Providers: A Comparison of 15 Leading Platforms
articles.summary: This article provides a comprehensive comparison of 15 leading cyber range platforms, evaluating their features, deployment models, and training capabilities. It serves as a guide for organizations to select appropriate simulated environments for security testing and workforce development.

articles.title: KDDI Data Breach Impacts up to 14.2 Million Email Accounts at Six ISPs
articles.summary: KDDI Corporation reported a data breach affecting up to 14.2 million email accounts across six Japanese internet service providers, caused by a vulnerability in third-party software.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 103
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware campaigns, including the compromise of 4,000 legacy routers for proxy attacks, a VBScript-based WhatsApp distribution scheme, and a new loader for CASTLESTEALER. It provides a curated overview of ongoing global cyber threats and technical research.

articles.title: Anonymous-Linked Hacktivist Aubrey Cottle Jailed Over Texas GOP Cyberattack
articles.summary: Canadian hacktivist Aubrey Cottle has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for his role in a 2021 cyberattack targeting the Texas GOP website. The incident highlights the legal consequences for individuals involved in politically motivated hacking activities.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 583 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This Security Affairs newsletter highlights recent cybersecurity developments, including a new FBI warning regarding Russian intelligence exploiting Signal recovery keys and ongoing attacks against the hospitality sector.

articles.title: Data breach exposes up to 14.2 million email logins at six ISPs
articles.summary: Japanese telecommunications giant KDDI Corporation suffered a data breach impacting an email system shared by five other ISPs, resulting in the exposure of up to 14.2 million user credentials.

articles.title: Week in review: Fortibleed campaign’s impact on orgs, Cisco Unified CM flaw exploited
articles.summary: The weekly report highlights the impact of the Fortibleed campaign on organizations and details the exploitation of a vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager. It also discusses privacy limitations regarding encrypted DNS traffic.

articles.title: Ukraine Says Russian Intelligence Used Fake Support Texts to Steal Messaging Credentials
articles.summary: The SSU and FBI have exposed a coordinated Russian intelligence campaign using fraudulent support messages to compromise the accounts of government officials, military personnel, and activists globally. The operation aimed to gain unauthorized access to sensitive messaging credentials to facilitate espionage.

articles.title: New FBI Alert: Russian Intelligence Uses Signal Recovery Keys to Access Messages
articles.summary: The FBI and CISA have issued an updated advisory warning that Russian intelligence services are exploiting Signal Backup Recovery Keys to compromise user message history and gain unauthorized account access. This campaign represents a shift in strategy toward long-term surveillance through advanced phishing tactics.

articles.title: Hospitality Sector Hit by Phishing Campaign Using Fake Guest Complaint Emails
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified a long-running phishing campaign targeting the hospitality sector that deploys TonRAT malware using persistent techniques. The attacks, active since April 2026, specifically exploit guest communication channels to compromise organizational environments.

articles.title: Clean GitHub repo tricks AI coding agents into running malware
articles.summary: Malicious actors are embedding hidden payloads in GitHub repositories that exploit automated AI coding agents to execute malware during routine repository setup. This supply chain attack technique evades both traditional security scanners and human oversight.

articles.title: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Sol With Restricted Access and Stronger Cyber Safeguards
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a restricted preview of its GPT-5.6 model series, including the flagship model 'Sol,' as part of a collaborative initiative with the U.S. government to enhance cybersecurity safeguards.

articles.title: DirtyClone: Fourth Linux Kernel Flaw in Six Weeks Escalates to Root
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a critical Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw, dubbed DirtyClone, that allows attackers to rewrite memory executables without leaving disk traces. This vulnerability is the fourth in the DirtyFrag family and carries a high CVSS score of 8.8.

articles.title: It's looking like a hot, messy summer for security teams as AI finds countless previously hidden vulns
articles.summary: The integration of AI into vulnerability discovery is rapidly uncovering vast numbers of previously unknown security flaws, placing significant strain on cybersecurity teams. This surge in identified vulnerabilities is expected to create a challenging and resource-intensive summer for security operations.

articles.title: FBI: Russian hackers now target Signal backup recovery keys
articles.summary: Russian intelligence services are utilizing phishing campaigns to harvest Signal Backup Recovery Keys, enabling the decryption and unauthorized access of users' historical messages. This evolution in tactics poses a significant risk to the privacy of encrypted communications.

articles.title: 8 Top SAST Tools for Polyglot Monorepos and Platform Engineering in 2026
articles.summary: This article evaluates eight leading Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools optimized for handling complex, multi-language monorepos and large-scale platform engineering environments in 2026. It focuses on features like incremental scanning, automated ownership, and custom rule management.

articles.title: Even the Secret Service won't use company-issued phones
articles.summary: The U.S. Secret Service is facing scrutiny for security failures, including the use of personal cell phones for sensitive missions and a lack of threat detection capabilities on government-issued devices. These operational lapses highlight significant vulnerabilities in the agency's mobile security infrastructure.

articles.title: CISA sets urgent deadline to fix Cisco flaw exploited in attacks
articles.summary: CISA has issued an urgent directive requiring federal agencies to patch an actively exploited vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager Server by this Sunday. The mandate aims to mitigate risks posed by ongoing attacks targeting the flaw.

articles.title: FBI Warns Russian Intelligence Hackers Target Signal Backup Recovery Keys
articles.summary: The FBI and CISA have issued an alert regarding Russian intelligence actors who are phishing Signal users to obtain their backup recovery keys, enabling unauthorized access to message history and account takeovers.

articles.title: Woodgnat Hackers Use Mistic RAT to Broker Access for Ransomware Gangs
articles.summary: The Woodgnat hacking group is utilizing the Mistic RAT to compromise corporate networks, acting as initial access brokers for various ransomware syndicates. This operational model significantly increases the risk of downstream ransomware attacks for the victimized organizations.

articles.title: ATF cancels controversial commercial geolocation contract
articles.summary: The ATF has terminated a controversial geolocation tracking contract, citing that the pilot tool failed to meet agency needs despite congressional reports indicating it was utilized in hundreds of active investigations.

articles.title: Threat Brief: Mitigating Large-Scale Credential Attacks
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides strategic guidance for defending against large-scale credential stuffing attacks specifically targeting security infrastructure devices.

articles.title: New SharkLoader Malware Deploys Cobalt Strike in StrikeShark Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new malware family named SharkLoader, which is being utilized in the StrikeShark campaign to deploy Cobalt Strike Beacons against government and diplomatic targets. The attack highlights a sophisticated threat actor targeting specific geopolitical entities.

articles.title: Polymarket customers lose $3 million in supply-chain attack
articles.summary: Polymarket suffered a $3 million loss after a third-party vendor breach allowed attackers to inject a malicious script into the platform's frontend. The company has committed to fully reimbursing all affected customers.

articles.title: Cybersecurity firms targeted by fraudulent OpenAI organization invites
articles.summary: Threat actors are impersonating legitimate organizations through fraudulent OpenAI invites to harvest sensitive corporate information from employees. This social engineering campaign exploits trust in AI platforms to gain unauthorized access to internal data.

articles.title: Chinese APT CL-STA-1062 Expands Attacks on Southeast Asian Critical Infrastructure With Custom Malware
articles.summary: Chinese-speaking threat actor CL-STA-1062 is conducting persistent cyber espionage operations targeting critical infrastructure in Southeast Asia using custom malware and a new backdoor dubbed TinyRCT.

articles.title: Chinese-Speaking APT Deploys New TinyRCT Backdoor in Southeast Asia Campaign
articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking APT actor identified as CL-STA-1062 is targeting Southeast Asian government and energy entities using a new custom backdoor named TinyRCT. The campaign represents a focused effort against critical infrastructure in the region.

articles.title: Amazon Q flaw let booby-trapped Git repos execute code, swipe cloud creds
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in Amazon Q allowed attackers to execute malicious code and steal cloud credentials through booby-trapped Git repository configurations. This flaw highlights broader security concerns regarding the execution of commands by AI coding assistants.

articles.title: Your First GRC Agent: A Red Teamer's Walkthrough
articles.summary: This article explores the implementation of an AI-driven GRC agent designed to automate control monitoring, evidence gap identification, and remediation task management for compliance professionals.

articles.title: New Linux pedit COW Exploit Enables Root Access by Poisoning Cached Binaries
articles.summary: A critical local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem allows unprivileged users to gain root access via an out-of-bounds write. A public exploit for this flaw, dubbed 'pedit COW,' is already available, posing an immediate risk to affected systems.

articles.title: Amazon Q Developer Flaw Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code via MCP Configs
articles.summary: A high-severity vulnerability in Amazon Q Developer allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code and steal cloud credentials by exploiting the application's handling of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Amazon has since released a patch to address the security flaw.

articles.title: Russia accuses Apple of ‘political censorship’ after VK apps removed from App Store
articles.summary: Apple removed several major Russian applications, including VKontakte, from its App Store, prompting accusations of political censorship from the Russian government.

articles.title: Turla group adds more malware to Russia’s espionage efforts against Ukraine
articles.summary: Google researchers have identified a new piece of malware called StockStay, which is being utilized by the Russian threat actor group Turla in its ongoing espionage campaigns against Ukraine.

articles.title: Russia used social engineering to breach prominent messaging accounts, Ukraine says
articles.summary: The Ukrainian Security Service reported that Russian operatives successfully compromised high-profile messaging accounts by masquerading as technical support staff to steal user credentials. The campaign relied on social engineering tactics rather than software exploits to gain unauthorized access.

articles.title: macOS Flaw Allowed Standard Users to Disable CrowdStrike and Kandji Security Tools
articles.summary: A macOS XPC vulnerability allowed unprivileged users to disable security software like CrowdStrike and Kandji. The vendors have since released patches to address the issue discovered by XM Cyber.

articles.title: CISA Adds Exploited PTC Windchill RCE Flaw to KEV as Web Shell Attacks Continue
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in PTC Windchill software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to ongoing active exploitation. The flaw is being leveraged by attackers to deploy web shells.

articles.title: Miasma campaign poisons 20-plus npm packages, hunts for developer secrets
articles.summary: The Miasma supply chain attack has compromised over 20 npm packages, including Leo Platform and RStreams, to steal developer credentials and target software maintainers. Microsoft has identified the campaign, which focuses on harvesting secrets through malicious package injections.

articles.title: FCC votes to toughen rules in bid to better protect undersea cables
articles.summary: The FCC has approved stricter regulations for undersea cable infrastructure, including a new requirement for submarine line terminal equipment operators to obtain licenses. This initiative aims to strengthen the security and oversight of critical telecommunications infrastructure.

articles.title: Proof’s x401 establishes an open protocol for AI agent identity and authorization
articles.summary: Proof has introduced x401, an open and issuer-neutral protocol designed to verify the identity and authorization of AI agents interacting with websites and APIs. The framework allows services to validate agent claims, such as organizational affiliation or signing authority, to ensure secure and trusted AI interactions.

articles.title: New DirtyClone Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Local Users Gain Root via Cloned Packets
articles.summary: The DirtyClone Linux kernel vulnerability allows local attackers to achieve root-level privilege escalation by corrupting file-backed memory through cloned network packets. Identified as CVE-2026-43503, the flaw has a CVSS score of 8.8 and is part of the DirtyFrag family.

articles.title: Critical open-source projects get a new security framework
articles.summary: The Linux Foundation has launched Akrites, a new industry initiative designed to streamline the remediation and disclosure process for vulnerabilities in critical open-source software. This framework addresses the increased risk posed by AI-accelerated exploitation timelines.

articles.title: Guardian Agents: The Next Layer of Identity Governance
articles.summary: The rapid integration of autonomous AI agents in enterprise environments is creating significant security gaps, as traditional identity governance frameworks are ill-equipped to manage machine-speed access. The headline highlights the urgent need for new governance structures to oversee these non-human actors.

articles.title: Activist Phone Hacked With Cellebrite After Russia Contract Cancellation
articles.summary: Russian authorities utilized Cellebrite forensic tools to bypass security measures on an activist's confiscated iPhone 12, despite the company's prior public commitment to terminate contracts with the country. This incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding the potential for forensic software misuse against political targets.

articles.title: Miasma Malware Targets npm Packages and GitHub Actions in Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: The Miasma malware family has expanded its supply chain attack campaign to compromise additional npm packages and GitHub Actions, while also extending its reach into the Go ecosystem.

articles.title: Synology issues critical fix for MailPlus Server vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Synology has released a critical security update for its MailPlus Server to address three vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to conduct unauthorized file operations, access internal services, and trigger denial-of-service attacks. Users are advised to apply the patch immediately to secure their private email infrastructure.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Cisco and PTC Windchill and FlexPLM flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include critical flaws affecting Cisco, PTC Windchill, and FlexPLM products. Organizations are urged to address these vulnerabilities to mitigate the risk of exploitation.

articles.title: Ransomware gangs find Europe’s weakest link in third-party suppliers
articles.summary: A 2026 report by Black Kite reveals that ransomware attacks against European organizations are rising, with threat actors increasingly targeting supply chains as their primary entry point. The study highlights the convergence of rising ransomware activity, vulnerable third-party suppliers, and complex regulatory landscapes.

articles.title: A decade of infrastructure development, one new name: Coinspaid Dev
articles.summary: The team behind Coinspaid Solutions has rebranded as Coinspaid Dev to focus on positioning themselves as a prominent voice in blockchain infrastructure engineering.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of Photo ZIP Phishing Campaign Targeting Hotels with Node.js Implant
articles.summary: Microsoft is tracking an ongoing phishing campaign targeting hospitality organizations across Europe and Asia that uses malicious ZIP files to deploy a Node.js implant. The threat actors remain unidentified, and their ultimate objectives for compromising front-desk systems are currently unknown.

articles.title: Mirage2FA phishing kit uses HTML smuggling to steal Microsoft 365 credentials
articles.summary: Fortra researchers have identified Mirage2FA, a sophisticated phishing kit that uses HTML smuggling and obfuscated JavaScript to bypass security filters and steal Microsoft 365 credentials during MFA processes. The campaign utilizes business-themed lures like fake invoices and payment requests to target users via email.

articles.title: Mystery hackers use novel SharkLoader dropper against governments, software devs
articles.summary: Kaspersky researchers have identified a global cyberattack campaign dubbed StrikeShark, which uses a new, previously unknown dropper called SharkLoader to target government and software development organizations. The sophisticated operation was uncovered during the investigation of a targeted attack on a diplomatic entity in Indonesia.

articles.title: Russia Used Cellebrite on Jailed Activist's iPhone Months After Sales Cutoff
articles.summary: Russian authorities successfully accessed an activist's iPhone using Cellebrite forensic tools months after the company officially ceased operations in Russia. The evidence, documented by Citizen Lab, highlights potential lapses in export compliance or the use of legacy hardware.

articles.title: Third-Party Breach at Polymarket Leads to $2.94M Crypto Theft
articles.summary: Polymarket experienced a security breach after attackers compromised a third-party vendor to inject malicious code into its website, resulting in the theft of $2.94 million in user funds.

articles.title: SIM-swapping gang busted in international police operation
articles.summary: Polish authorities, in collaboration with the FBI and HSI, dismantled an international cybercrime gang responsible for SIM-swapping attacks, cryptocurrency theft, and money laundering. Four suspects were arrested as part of an ongoing investigation into the group's organized cyber operations.

articles.title: ZeroTier Quantum RC2 brings post-quantum security closer to general availability
articles.summary: ZeroTier has released the second release candidate for its quantum-secure networking platform, aligning with upcoming U.S. government post-quantum cryptography standards. This move aims to protect network traffic against future threats posed by advanced quantum computing.

articles.title: ThreatModeler introduces Nexus to automate threat modeling with AI governance
articles.summary: ThreatModeler has launched Nexus, an agentic threat modeling platform that leverages AI governance to automate security architecture analysis throughout the software development lifecycle.

articles.title: macOS.Gaslight: North Korea-Linked Malware That Tries to Gaslight the Analyst
articles.summary: North Korean threat actors have developed a Rust-based macOS implant called macOS.Gaslight that utilizes prompt injection payloads to deceive AI-driven security analysis tools. The malware was discovered after an Apple XProtect update and represents a novel tactic in anti-forensic techniques.

articles.title: Google Details Turla's New STOCKSTAY Backdoor Used in Ukraine Espionage Attacks
articles.summary: Google Threat Intelligence has identified a new .NET backdoor named STOCKSTAY, developed by the Russian-linked threat actor Turla for use in espionage operations against Ukrainian government and military entities. The malware is part of an ongoing campaign targeting organizations with interests in Italian foreign policy.

articles.title: Microsoft gives Windows 10 users an unexpected extra year of free security updates
articles.summary: Microsoft has extended the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10 consumers by an additional year, providing security coverage until October 12, 2027. This update allows users to maintain device security longer than previously anticipated without immediate forced upgrades.

articles.title: Security boss thought MFA would be too much security
articles.summary: A security executive chose to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) protocols for leadership, citing concerns over excessive security despite enforcing them for the rest of the workforce. This decision highlights a hypocritical 'rules for thee, not for me' approach that undermines organizational security posture.

articles.title: A privacy-first take on local malware analysis
articles.summary: The article discusses the privacy risks of uploading suspicious files to public malware repositories, where attackers can track the distribution of their own tools. It advocates for local malware analysis techniques to maintain operational security.

articles.title: New infosec products of the month: June 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights several new cybersecurity product releases for June 2026, including Asimily's new Segmentation Orchestration tool for automated device risk management. It provides a roundup of updates from various vendors aimed at enhancing security operations and asset visibility.

articles.title: Chinese cybersecurity company claims it’s built a better-than-Mythos bug finder
articles.summary: Qihoo 360, a Chinese cybersecurity firm restricted by the US, claims to have developed an automated vulnerability discovery tool that surpasses Mythos, positioning it as a countermeasure against AI-driven cyber weaponization.

articles.title: Anthropic is testing desktop-like Claude Cowork for mobile
articles.summary: Anthropic is testing a 'Claude Cowork' feature for mobile devices, enabling users to manage long-running AI tasks directly from their phones. This expansion increases the accessibility and mobile integration of their AI agent capabilities.

articles.title: Poland busts SIM-swapping gang tied to millions in crypto theft
articles.summary: Polish authorities have arrested four individuals involved in a cybercrime group that utilized SIM-swapping and email hijacking to steal millions in cryptocurrency. The operation focused on compromising telecommunications partners to facilitate these fraudulent attacks.
